title: Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/01 - Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) Analysis.md
goal: The goal of a Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) analysis is to determine the direct costs associated with delivering a SaaS product to customers.
dataRequired: Hosting and infrastructure costs (e.g., cloud services, servers)
Customer support costs (e.g., salaries, support software)
Software licenses or third-party integrations (e.g., APIs, payment gateways)
Data storage and bandwidth costs
Direct labor costs (e.g., salaries of technical support or operations staW)
improve: Negotiate better rates with third-party providers
Optimize data storage and bandwidth usage

title: Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) Growth Rate
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/02 - Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) Growth Rate.md
goal: The goal of Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) Growth Rate analysis is to measure the percentage increase (or decrease) in MRR over a period of time.
dataRequired: MRR at the start of the month
MRR at the end of the month
MRR from new customers acquired during the month
MRR lost from churned customers
MRR expansion from existing customers (e.g., upgrades or cross-sells)
MRR contraction from existing customers (e.g., downgrades)

title: Annual Contract Value (ACV) Analysis
goal: The goal of Annual Contract Value (ACV) analysis is to determine the average annual revenue generated per customer contract.
dataRequired: Total contract value for each customer over the contract duration
Length of each customer contract (in years)
Number of customers or contracts being analyzed

formulas.source: ACV = Total Contract Value / Contract Length (in years)

title: Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/04 - Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) Analysis.md
goal: The goal of Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) analysis is to measure the average monthly revenue generated from each customer.
dataRequired: Total revenue for the selected period (typically monthly or quarterly)
Total number of active users (customers) during that period

formulas.source: ARPU = Total Revenue / Total Number of Active Users

title: Deferred Revenue Analysis
goal: The goal of Deferred Revenue Analysis is to assess the revenue that a SaaS company has received in advance for services it has not yet delivered.
dataRequired: Customer payments received in advance for subscriptions or services
Length of the subscription period (monthly, quarterly, annually)
Revenue recognized over time for those subscriptions
Start and end dates of each contract
improve: Monitor cash ﬂow vs. deferred revenue

formulas.source: Deferred Revenue = Total Payment Received - Revenue Recognized to Date
formulas.step: Calculate Deferred Revenue for each customer

title: Expansion Revenue Analysis
goal: The goal of Expansion Revenue Analysis is to measure the additional revenue generated from existing customers through upsells, cross-sells, or upgrades over a speciﬁc period.
dataRequired: Total Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) or Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) from existing customers at the start of the period
Revenue added through upsells, cross-sells, or plan upgrades during the period
Number of customers who upgraded or expanded their services
**Optional:** Breakdowns by customer segment, product, or service
improve: OKer tiered pricing and premium features

formulas.source: Expansion Revenue (%) = (Revenue from Expansions / Revenue at Start of Period) x 100
formulas.step: Calculate the percentage of expansion revenue

title: Revenue Backlog
goal: The goal of the Revenue Backlog analysis is to quantify the committed but unrecognized revenue that a SaaS company has secured from customers, typically through long-term contracts or multi- year subscriptions.
dataRequired: **Total contracted revenue:** The total value of all active contracts or subscriptions that are yet to be fully recognized as revenue.
**Revenue recognized to date:** The portion of contracted revenue that has already been recognized as revenue.
**Remaining contract duration:** The time remaining on active customer contracts, which helps estimate when the backlog will be recognized.
**Customer segmentation (optional):** Data on backlog by customer segment or contract size to identify concentration risks or growth opportunities.
improve: Align sales and customer success teams

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Revenue Backlog
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Revenue Backlog = Total Contracted Revenue - Revenue Recognized to Date

formulas.output: o    If relevant, use the formula: Revenue Backlog per Period
formulas.source: o    If relevant, use the formula: Revenue Backlog per Period = Total Revenue Backlog / Number of Remaining Periods

title: Revenue Concentration
goal: The goal of the Revenue Concentration analysis is to determine how dependent a SaaS company is on its top customers for revenue generation.
dataRequired: **Total revenue:** The total revenue generated by the company during a speciﬁc period (e.g., monthly or annually).
**Revenue per customer:** The revenue generated from each individual customer or account during the same period.
**Top customers:** The number or percentage of customers contributing the most revenue (e.g., top 5, top 10, or top 20 customers).
improve: Develop long-term contracts or subscription commitments

formulas.source: Revenue Concentration (%) = (Revenue from Top Customers / Total Revenue) x 100

title: Revenue Forecasting Accuracy
goal: The goal of the Revenue Forecasting Accuracy analysis is to measure how closely a SaaS company’s actual revenue aligns with its forecasted revenue.
dataRequired: **Forecasted revenue:** The revenue that was predicted or forecasted for a given period (e.g., monthly, quarterly, or annually).
**Actual revenue:** The revenue that was actually generated during the same period.
**Historical revenue forecasts and actuals:** Historical data on revenue forecasts and actual results to compare and evaluate trends over time.
**Segmentation data (optional):** Segmented forecasts and actuals by product, region, or customer type to assess forecasting accuracy across different business areas.
improve: Account for churn and customer retention rates

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Forecasting Error
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Forecasting Error = Actual Revenue - Forecasted Revenue

title: Discount Rate Impact
goal: The goal of the Discount Rate Impact analysis is to evaluate how discounting affects a SaaS company's overall revenue, proﬁtability, and customer acquisition efforts.
dataRequired: **Total revenue:** The total revenue generated over a speciﬁc period (e.g., monthly, quarterly, or annually).
**Revenue from discounted deals:** The revenue generated from customers who received a discount during the same period.
**Average discount rate:** The average percentage discount applied to deals during the period.
**Customer acquisition and retention data:** The number of customers acquired or retained through discounted offers.
**Gross margin:** The gross margin percentage to evaluate the proﬁtability impact of discounts.

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Average Discount Rate (%)
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Average Discount Rate (%) = (Total Discount Amount / Total Original Contract Value) x 100

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Revenue Loss
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Revenue Loss = Total Original Contract Value - Revenue from Discounted Deals

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Adjusted Gross Proﬁt
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Adjusted Gross Proﬁt = Revenue from Discounted Deals x Gross Margin

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Customer Acquisition/Retention via Discounts (%)
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Customer Acquisition/Retention via Discounts (%) = (Number of Customers Acquired/Retained via Discounts / Total Number of Customers Acquired/Retained) x 100

title: Revenue per Employee Analysis
goal: The goal of Revenue per Employee analysis is to measure the efficiency and productivity of a SaaS company by calculating how much revenue is generated for every employee.
dataRequired: Total revenue for the period (e.g., annual or quarterly revenue)
Total number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees during the same period
improve: Focus on customer success and retention

formulas.source: Revenue per Employee = Total Revenue / Total Number of Employees

title: Freemium to Paid Conversion Rate Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/12 - Freemium to Paid Conversion Rate Analysis.md
goal: The goal of Freemium to Paid Conversion Rate analysis is to measure the percentage of users who move from the free (freemium) version of a SaaS product to a paid subscription.
dataRequired: Total number of freemium users during the period
Number of freemium users who converted to paid plans during the period
Timeframe for conversion (e.g., monthly or quarterly)
improve: Provide customer support for freemium users
Segment users and tailor conversion strategies

variables: Number of Users Converted to Paid Plans
formulas.source: Freemium to Paid Conversion Rate (%) = (Number of Users Converted to Paid Plans / Total Number of Freemium Users) x 100
formulas.step: Calculate the Freemium to Paid Conversion Rate

title: Lead-to-Customer Conversion Rate Analysis
goal: The goal of Lead-to-Customer Conversion Rate analysis is to measure the percentage of leads that successfully convert into paying customers.
dataRequired: Total number of leads generated during the period (e.g., month, quarter)
Number of leads that converted into paying customers during the same period
Timeframe for conversion (e.g., monthly or quarterly)

variables: Number of Leads Converted to Customers
formulas.source: Lead-to-Customer Conversion Rate (%) = (Number of Leads Converted to Customers / Total Number of Leads) x 100

title: Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) Analysis
goal: The goal of Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) analysis is to determine the average cost incurred by a SaaS company to acquire a new customer.
dataRequired: Total sales and marketing expenses for a given period (e.g., monthly or quarterly)
Number of new customers acquired during the same period

formulas.source: CAC = Total Sales and Marketing Expenses / Number of New Customers Acquired

title: Sales Cycle Length Analysis
goal: The goal of Sales Cycle Length analysis is to determine the average time it takes for a lead to progress from initial contact to becoming a paying customer.
dataRequired: Date of ﬁrst contact with the lead (or when the lead entered the pipeline)
Date the lead converted to a paying customer
Number of leads and closed deals during the analysis period
improve: Shorten free trials or demo periods

formulas.source: Sales Cycle Length = Date of Conversion - Date of First Contact
formulas.step: Calculate the sales cycle length for each deal

variables: Sum of Sales Cycle Lengths for All Deals
formulas.source: Average Sales Cycle Length = (Sum of Sales Cycle Lengths for All Deals) / (Number of Deals Closed)
formulas.step: Calculate the average sales cycle length

title: Sales Efficiency Ratio
goal: The goal of the Sales Efficiency Ratio, often referred to as the Magic Number in the SaaS industry, is to assess the effectiveness of a company's sales and marketing spend by measuring how much incremental revenue is generated for every dollar invested in acquiring customers.
dataRequired: **Previous quarter’s revenue (ARR):** The annual recurring revenue (ARR) at the start of the period being measured.
**Current quarter’s revenue (ARR):** The ARR at the end of the period.
**Sales and marketing expenses:** Total amount spent on sales and marketing during the period (typically quarterly).

title: Payback Period on Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/17 - Payback Period on Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC).md
goal: The goal of the Payback Period on CAC analysis is to determine the amount of time it takes for a SaaS company to recover the costs associated with acquiring a new customer.
dataRequired: **Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC):** The total cost of acquiring a customer, including sales, marketing, and onboarding expenses.
**Average Revenue Per User (ARPU):** The average amount of revenue generated per customer in a speciﬁc period (e.g., monthly or annually).
**Gross margin percentage:** To account for the costs associated with delivering the service and ensure that only proﬁts contribute to covering CAC.

formulas.source: o    Use the formula: CAC = Total Sales and Marketing Expenses / Number of New Customers Acquired
o    Use the formula: ARPU = Total Revenue / Total Number of Customers

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Gross Margin-Adjusted ARPU
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Gross Margin-Adjusted ARPU = ARPU x Gross Margin
o    Payback Period (months) = CAC / Gross Margin-Adjusted ARPU

title: Engagement-to-Subscription Rate
goal: The goal of the Engagement-to-Subscription Rate analysis is to measure how effectively a SaaS company is converting engaged users (e.g., free trial users or freemium customers) into paying subscribers.
dataRequired: **Number of engaged users:** The total number of users who actively engage with the product during a given period (e.g., free trial users, freemium users).
**Number of users who convert to a paid subscription:** The total number of users who subscribe to a paid plan during the same period.
**User engagement metrics (optional):** Detailed engagement data such as frequency of use, feature adoption, or time spent on the platform to better understand patterns that drive conversions.
improve: Enhance the free trial or freemium experience
Improve user engagement during the free period
Use data to identify high-intent users

variables: Number of Users Who Convert to Paid Subscription
formulas.source: Engagement-to-Subscription Rate (%) = (Number of Users Who Convert to Paid Subscription / Number of Engaged Users) x 100

title: Partner Ecosystem Contribution
goal: The goal of the Partner Ecosystem Contribution analysis is to measure the extent to which a SaaS company’s partners (e.g., resellers, consultants, systems integrators, and technology partners) contribute to the company’s overall revenue and growth.
dataRequired: **Total revenue:** The total revenue generated by the company over a speciﬁc period (e.g., monthly, quarterly, or annually).
**Revenue from partners:** The total revenue generated through partners, broken down by partner type (e.g., resellers, systems integrators) and individual partners, if available.
**Number of customers acquired through partners:** The number of customers brought in by the partner network.
**Partner-related costs (optional):** Costs associated with managing the partner ecosystem, including commissions, incentives, and marketing spend.

formulas.source: Partner Revenue Contribution (%) = (Revenue from Partners / Total Revenue) x 100

variables: Number of Customers Acquired via Partners
formulas.source: Partner Customer Acquisition Rate (%) = (Number of Customers Acquired via Partners / Total Number of Customers Acquired) x 100

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Partner Proﬁt
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Partner Proﬁt = Revenue from Partners - Partner-Related Costs

title: Customer Segmentation Analysis
goal: The goal of Customer Segmentation Analysis is to divide a SaaS company's customer base into distinct groups based on shared characteristics, behaviors, or needs.
dataRequired: Customer demographic data (e.g., company size, industry, geography)
Behavioral data (e.g., product usage frequency, feature adoption)
Financial data (e.g., Average Revenue Per User (ARPU), Customer Lifetime Value (CLV))
Customer satisfaction data (e.g., Net Promoter Score (NPS), support interactions)
Sales and marketing data (e.g., lead source, customer acquisition cost)
improve: Optimize product features for diKerent segments
Create targeted upsell and cross-sell campaigns

formulas.output: o    Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) per segment: ARPU
formulas.source: o    Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) per segment: ARPU = Total Revenue from Segment / Number of Customers in Segment

formulas.output: o    Churn rate per segment: Churn Rate
variables: Number of Customers Lost in Segment
Number of Customers at Start of Period in Segment
formulas.source: o    Churn rate per segment: Churn Rate = (Number of Customers Lost in Segment / Number of Customers at Start of Period in Segment) x 100

title: Contract Renewal Rate Analysis
goal: The goal of Contract Renewal Rate analysis is to measure the percentage of customers who renew their contracts at the end of their subscription period.
dataRequired: Number of contracts up for renewal during a speciﬁc period
Number of contracts that were successfully renewed during the same period
Total number of customers at the start of the period
Total number of contracts expiring (for customers not renewing)

variables: Total Number of Contracts Up for Renewal
formulas.source: Contract Renewal Rate (%) = (Number of Contracts Renewed / Total Number of Contracts Up for Renewal) x 100

title: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) Analysis
goal: The goal of Net Revenue Retention (NRR) analysis is to measure the total revenue retained from existing customers over a speciﬁc period, accounting for customer expansion, downgrades, and churn.
dataRequired: Total Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR) or Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) from existing customers at the start of the period
Revenue added from customer expansions (upsells, cross-sells) during the period
Revenue lost from customer downgrades during the period
Revenue lost due to customer churn (cancellations) during the period
improve: Focus on customer success and product adoption
OKer tiered pricing and value-added features
Analyze reasons for downgrades and churn
Segment customers based on value and potential

title: Churn Rate Analysis
goal: The goal of Churn Rate Analysis is to measure the rate at which customers or revenue are being lost over a speciﬁc period of time.
dataRequired: Number of customers at the start of the period
Number of customers lost during the period
Total revenue at the start of the period
Total revenue lost due to churned customers or downgrades during the period
Total revenue expansion from upgrades or cross-sells during the period (for net revenue churn)
improve: Collect and act on customer feedback

variables: Number of Customers Lost During the Period
Number of Customers at the Start of the Period
formulas.source: Customer Churn Rate (%) = (Number of Customers Lost During the Period / Number of Customers at the Start of the Period) x 100

variables: Total Revenue at the Start of the Period
formulas.source: Revenue Churn Rate (%) = (Revenue Lost During the Period / Total Revenue at the Start of the Period) x 100

title: Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) Analysis
goal: The goal of Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) analysis is to estimate the total revenue a SaaS company can expect to generate from a single customer over the entire duration of their relationship.
dataRequired: Average Revenue Per User (ARPU)
Average customer lifespan (how long a customer remains active, in months or years)
Customer retention rate (optional)
Gross margin percentage (optional for more reﬁned CLV calculation)
improve: Increase customer satisfaction and product usage

formulas.source: ARPU = Total Revenue from Customers / Total Number of Customers
formulas.step: Calculate the Average Revenue Per User (ARPU)

formulas.source: Average Customer Lifespan = 1 / Monthly Churn Rate
CLV = ARPU x Average Customer Lifespan
CLV = (ARPU x Average Customer Lifespan) x Gross Margin
formulas.step: Reﬁne the CLV by incorporating gross margin (optional)

title: First Contact Resolution (FCR) Rate
goal: The goal of the First Contact Resolution (FCR) Rate analysis is to measure the percentage of customer support issues resolved during the initial interaction with the support team.
dataRequired: **Total number of customer support cases:** The total number of cases or tickets handled by the support team during a speciﬁed time period (e.g., monthly or quarterly).
**Number of cases resolved on ﬁrst contact:** The number of support cases resolved during the initial interaction without requiring follow-up communication.
**Customer feedback (optional):** Data on customer satisfaction or feedback regarding whether the issue was fully resolved during the ﬁrst contact, if available.
improve: Empower support agents with the right tools
Monitor and reﬁne common issue workﬂows

formulas.output: o    Use the following formula to calculate the FCR rate: FCR Rate (%)
variables: Number of Cases Resolved on First Contact
Total Number of Customer Support Cases
formulas.source: o    Use the following formula to calculate the FCR rate: FCR Rate (%) = (Number of Cases Resolved on First Contact / Total Number of Customer Support Cases) x 100

title: Customer Advocacy or Net Promoter Score (NPS)
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/26 - Customer Advocacy or Net Promoter Score (NPS).md
goal: The goal of the Customer Advocacy or Net Promoter Score (NPS) analysis is to measure customer satisfaction and loyalty by determining how likely customers are to recommend a SaaS company’s product or service to others.
dataRequired: **NPS survey responses:** Responses to the NPS question: “On a scale of 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend our product to a friend or colleague?”
**Total number of respondents:** The number of customers who participated in the NPS survey.
**Customer segmentation (optional):** Segment NPS scores by customer type (e.g., small business, enterprise), product, or region to analyze advocacy across different groups.
improve: Monitor and track NPS over time

formulas.source: o    Use the formula: NPS = Promoter Percentage - Detractor Percentage

title: Customer Success Team Efficiency
goal: The goal of the Customer Success Team Efficiency analysis is to measure the workload and effectiveness of the customer success team, typically by analyzing the ratio of customers to each Customer Success Manager (CSM).
dataRequired: **Total number of customers:** The number of active customers that the customer success team is currently managing.
**Number of Customer Success Managers (CSMs):** The total number of CSMs on the team.
**Customer segmentation (optional):** Customer data by segment (e.g., small business, enterprise) to calculate efficiency for different customer types, as workload may vary by customer segment.
**Customer satisfaction (optional):** Data on customer satisfaction or Net Promoter Score (NPS) to evaluate the quality of support provided by CSMs.
improve: Invest in CSM training and resources
Expand the team as the customer base grows

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Customers per CSM
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Customers per CSM = Total Number of Customers / Number of CSMs

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Customers per CSM by Segment
variables: Total Number of Customers in Segment
Number of CSMs Assigned to that Segment
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Customers per CSM by Segment = Total Number of Customers in Segment / Number of CSMs Assigned to that Segment

title: Customer Support Efficiency Analysis
goal: The goal of Customer Support Efficiency analysis is to assess how effectively a SaaS company’s customer support team resolves customer issues.
dataRequired: Total number of support tickets opened during a speciﬁc period
Number of unique customers served during the same period
Average time taken to resolve support tickets (resolution time)
Number of support agents (optional, for staffing analysis)
Customer satisfaction data (optional, e.g., CSAT or NPS scores post-resolution)

formulas.source: Tickets per Customer = Total Number of Tickets / Total Number of Unique Customers

variables: Total Time to Resolve All Tickets
formulas.source: Average Resolution Time = Total Time to Resolve All Tickets / Total Number of Tickets Resolved

title: Platform and Ecosystem Integration Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/29 - Platform and Ecosystem Integration Analysis.md
goal: The goal of Platform and Ecosystem Integration Analysis is to evaluate how well a SaaS product integrates with other software platforms and tools within a customer's technology ecosystem.
dataRequired: Number of integrations used by customers
Types of platforms and tools the SaaS product integrates with (e.g., CRM, ERP, collaboration tools)
Usage data for each integration (e.g., how frequently the integrations are used)
Customer feedback on integration satisfaction and ease of use
Performance metrics for integrations (e.g., uptime, error rates)

formulas.output: Average Number of Integrations per Customer
formulas.source: Average Number of Integrations per Customer = Total Number of Integrations Used / Total Number
formulas.step: Analyze the number of integrations per customer

title: Time to First Value Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/30 - Time to First Value Analysis.md
goal: The goal of Time to First Value (TTFV) analysis is to measure how long it takes for a new customer to realize their ﬁrst meaningful success with a SaaS product.
dataRequired: Customer sign-up date or start date
Date when the customer ﬁrst achieves a key success metric or milestone (e.g., completing a setup, launching their ﬁrst campaign, or reaching a usage goal)
Total number of customers during the analysis period
Deﬁnition of "ﬁrst value" (based on product-speciﬁc metrics or goals)
**Optional:** Segmentation by customer size, industry, or product usage
improve: Track product usage and identify friction points

formulas.source: Time to First Value (TTFV) = Date of First Value - Customer Sign-up Date
formulas.step: Calculate the Time to First Value (TTFV) for each customer

formulas.source: Average TTFV = Total TTFV for All Customers / Total Number of Customers

title: User Onboarding Efficiency
goal: The goal of User Onboarding Efficiency analysis is to measure how effectively a SaaS company guides new users through the onboarding process, ensuring they reach key milestones that demonstrate the value of the product.
dataRequired: **Number of users starting the onboarding process:** The total number of users who begin the onboarding process.
**Number of users completing the onboarding process:** The total number of users who complete the onboarding steps and reach activation.
**Time to activation:** The average time taken for a user to complete onboarding and begin using the product effectively.

**Milestones or key actions:** Speciﬁc actions or features that users must engage with to be considered fully onboarded (e.g., completing a setup tutorial, sending their ﬁrst email, or uploading their ﬁrst ﬁle).
**Churn during onboarding:** The number of users who churn during the onboarding process.
improve: Monitor onboarding funnel and ﬁx drop-oK points

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Onboarding Completion Rate (%)
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Onboarding Completion Rate (%) = (Number of Users Completing Onboarding / Number of Users Starting Onboarding) x 100

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Average Time to Activation
variables: Total Time Taken for All Users to Activate
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Average Time to Activation = Total Time Taken for All Users to Activate / Number of Users Activated

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: Onboarding Churn Rate (%)
variables: Number of Users Who Churn During Onboarding
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: Onboarding Churn Rate (%) = (Number of Users Who Churn During Onboarding / Number of Users Starting Onboarding) x 100

title: Product Usage by Tier or Plan
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/32 - Product Usage by Tier or Plan.md
goal: The goal of the Product Usage by Tier or Plan analysis is to evaluate how users across different pricing tiers or subscription plans engage with a SaaS product.
dataRequired: **Number of users by tier or plan:** Total number of users subscribed to each pricing tier (e.g., Basic, Pro, Enterprise).
**Product usage data per tier:** Metrics on how users within each tier are engaging with product features (e.g., number of sessions, feature usage, or time spent).
**Feature availability by tier:** A list of features available in each pricing tier to compare feature utilization against access.
**Revenue per tier:** Total revenue generated by each tier, if relevant to assess revenue contribution versus usage.

formulas.output: o    Use the formula for each tier: Feature Usage by Tier (%)
variables: Number of Features Used by Tier
Number of Available Features in Tier
formulas.source: o    Use the formula for each tier: Feature Usage by Tier (%) = (Number of Features Used by Tier / Number of Available Features in Tier) x 100

title: Usage and Engagement Metrics Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/33 - Usage and Engagement Metrics Analysis.md
goal: The goal of Usage and Engagement Metrics analysis is to measure how often and how deeply customers are using a SaaS product.
dataRequired: Number of active users (daily, weekly, or monthly)
Number of logins or sessions per user
Key product feature usage frequency (e.g., how often users access core features)
Duration of each session
Number of actions performed during each session (e.g., number of tasks completed, messages sent)
User segmentation (optional) to analyze behavior across different customer segments

formulas.source: DAU/MAU Ratio = (Daily Active Users / Monthly Active Users) x 100
Average Sessions per User = Total Number of Sessions / Number of Active Users

title: Product Stickiness and Retention Rate Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/34 - Product Stickiness and Retention Rate Analysis.md
goal: The goal of Product Stickiness and Retention Rate analysis is to measure how frequently customers use a SaaS product and how likely they are to stay as paying customers over time.
dataRequired: Daily Active Users (DAU)
Monthly Active Users (MAU)
Number of customers at the start and end of a period
Number of customers lost (churned) during the period
Usage frequency data (e.g., login activity, feature engagement)
improve: Improve customer support and success eKorts
Gather feedback and address pain points
Launch new features or updates based on user needs

formulas.source: Product Stickiness (%) = (DAU / MAU) x 100

variables: Number of Customers at End of Period
Number of Customers at Start of Period
formulas.source: Retention Rate (%) = (Number of Customers at End of Period / Number of Customers at Start of Period) x 100

title: Time to Value (TTV) for Customers
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/saas/35 - Time to Value (TTV) for Customers.md
goal: The goal of the Time to Value (TTV) analysis is to measure the time it takes for new customers to realize the core value of a SaaS product after they ﬁrst start using it.
dataRequired: **Start date of customer onboarding:** The date when the customer starts using the product (e.g., when they sign up or complete onboarding).

**Milestone for value realization:** A key action or milestone that indicates the customer has realized the product’s core value (e.g., completing a setup, achieving a speciﬁc result, or using a core feature).
**Date of value realization:** The date when the customer reaches the deﬁned milestone.
**Customer segments (optional):** Segmentation data for different types of customers (e.g., small business, enterprise) to compare TTV across segments.
improve: Use product tours and in-app guidance
Segment onboarding for diKerent customer types

formulas.output: o    Use the formula: TTV (in days)
formulas.source: o    Use the formula: TTV (in days) = Date of Value Realization - Date of Onboarding Start
